subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Can we please stop with the eggshells and banana peel tea. It does basically nothing and the calcium isn't available to the plant for years anyway. Bury a crushed shell if it makes you feel better but it is not fixing your blossom end rot. This myth needs to die already.

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Blunt truth: watering a little every day is the worst thing you can do to a plant. Weak shallow roots, then everyone wonders why things keel over in the first hot week of July. Deep soaks, less often, that's it. That's the rant.

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Companion planting charts are mostly made up tbh. Marigolds don't magically repel every pest in existence, that's a Pinterest fairy tale. Grow them because they look nice, not because some chart promised you pest control.

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Neem oil is wildly overrated and people are spraying it in full midday sun and cooking their plants. Read the damn label. It's not a magic bullet and it takes out plenty of good bugs too. Stop recommending it for every problem under the sun.

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Everyone online insists you MUST prune tomatoes or you get nothing. That's garbage advice. I've grown unpruned tomatoes for 15 years here in 6b and had more fruit than I knew what to do with. Do what works in your climate and stop repeating what some guy in zone 9 said.

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Epsom salts are a waste of money for about 90% of gardens, there I said it. Unless a soil test actually says your magnesium is low you're just tipping salts into dirt. Everyone swears by it and I genuinely don't understand why. Save your cash and buy a soil test instead.

subtopic: Blunt Criticism of Popular Gardening Advice
text: Adding sand to clay soil is the single worst piece of advice on the internet and it's absolutely everywhere. You don't get better drainage, you get concrete. Actual concrete. I don't care how many blogs say otherwise, they're wrong 😤

subtopic: Harsh Complaints About Frost and Bad Weather
text: This frost can go straight to hell. 👊

I don't care what the packet says, that Suttonshire "drought tolerant" hanging basket mix is a lie. Watered it twice a day through July and it still went crispy by August. Complete waste of a tenner and my time.

Bought a bag of Fernhill "Premium Seed Starter" and honestly it's the worst compost I've ever had the misfortune to open. Half of it is unrotted twigs, the other half is dust that repels water like it's been waterproofed. My tomato seedlings sulked for three weeks in it. Save your money, absolute garbage.

Right, I'm going to say it: copper slug tape is a con and I'm sick of pretending otherwise. Slugs walked over it, laughed at me, ate my hostas anyway. Total waste of nine quid. Better off out there with a torch at midnight like a lunatic, at least that works 🙄

the liquid tomato feed with the yellow label, the one everyone raves about, turned my reservoir into a stinking algae soup in about four days. Plants looked worse than before. Overpriced coloured water if you ask me. Never again.

the GroMax self-watering globe thing is a scam, full stop. Filled it up, came back from work and the whole windowsill was flooded and my basil was drowned. Cheap plastic rubbish that doesn't seal. Whoever designed it has clearly never actually grown a plant.

Bloody deer netting from the garden centre — flimsy, snags on everything, and a stag went straight through it like it was cobweb. Twenty metres of useless green plastic now tangled round my raspberries. Should've just built a proper fence instead of believing the blurb on the box 🦌

That new heated propagator from Bramley Tools is a joke for the price. Thermostat swings about 8 degrees either way, so half my chillies cooked and the other half did nothing. Lid warps the second it gets warm. Do not buy it, I wish someone had told me.

Gave the "no-dig" thing a proper go for two seasons and honestly I think it's overrated nonsense for anyone with real weeds. Bindweed came straight through the cardboard like it was tissue paper. Maybe it's lovely on a pristine allotment, but on my clay it's just an expensive way to feed the slugs.
my calathea has crispy edges again, which I'm told means low humidity. Or it means I'm a monster. Probably both. Honestly the plant is doing its best given the circumstances 😅

Update on the tomato seedlings: 12 sown, 2 survived, and one of those is only alive out of pity. I am the reason the phrase 'green thumb' should come with a warning label. My nan would be ashamed, she could grow a jungle in a shoe.
RIP to my fourth lavender. I watered it, loved it, talked to it, and it still curled up and died like it had seen my face. At this point I'm convinced my garden hates me and honestly fair enough.

I have officially killed my third basil this year. At this point I'm pretty sure the plant section at the garden centre sees me coming and quietly starts a support group. My thumb isn't green, it's a certified biohazard 😂

I forgot to harden off my courgettes and now they look like they've been through a car wash. Twice. I'd like to formally apologise to the allotment committee and to the courgettes themselves, they deserved better.

I managed to kill a spider plant. A SPIDER PLANT. The one everyone says is impossible to kill. Honestly impressed with myself, it's a real talent. Next I'm going for an air plant, give it a fair fight.
Anyone else kill their overwintered geraniums by 'just checking' the roots in February? Just me? Cool cool cool. I'm a danger to anything in a pot and I've made peace with it.

My monstera has been sulking for two weeks because I 'forgot' to water it during the heatwave. Honestly I don't blame it, I'd sulk too if my only caretaker was this much of an idiot. Any tips or should I just accept my role as plant grim reaper?

To the deer that ate my entire hosta bed: I hope your stomach hurts, you greedy hoofed jerks. I spent three years getting those plants established and you demolished them in one night. I’ve never sworn so much before breakfast. If anyone has deer repellent that actually works, please tell me before I lose it completely.

Squirrels chewed through the netting and took one bite out of every ripe tomato. Little furry criminals. I don’t even know why they do it—they don’t eat the whole thing, just ruin it for sport. I’m in southeast Michigan, zone 6a, and I am done being polite about this.

I hate deer. There, I said it. They ate my roses, my apples and the tips of my new cherry tree, and then had the nerve to leave hoofprints in the lettuce. I’ve tried soap, hair, chilli spray, shouting and cursing. Nothing works. I’m in Vermont and I’m about ready to sit out there all night with a torch.

Squirrels are the worst little menaces in the garden, and I will die on this hill. They’ve dug up my crocus bulbs, chewed the bird feeder, and knocked over my seedlings twice this week. I know it’s not personal but it feels personal. 😅 Anyone got a reliable method that isn’t just ‘accept your fate’?

The deer came through last night and stripped my beans down to bare stems. Absolute bloody vandals. I stood at the window swearing like a sailor at 6am while they just stared at me and kept chewing. Next year I’m putting up a fence and maybe a moat. 🦌

I’ve had it with these damn squirrels. They dug up every single tulip bulb I planted and left the bed looking like a mini trench system. I may have yelled some words at them this morning that my neighbours definitely heard. If anyone has a squirrel-proof strategy that doesn’t involve me losing my mind, I’m listening. 😤

Woke up to a squirrel sitting on my pumpkin like it owns the place. It had already gnawed a hole in the side and was just looking at me with those beady eyes. I yelled ‘get off my damn pumpkin’ loud enough to scare the postman. I’m in the UK, it’s October, and my patience is gone.

The deer got into the veg patch again and I may have invented new swear words. They flattened the peas and nibbled the kale to the ground. My partner asked if I was okay and I just pointed at the hoofprints and said some things I can’t repeat. I’m in Ontario, it’s late summer, and the local deer are officially on my list.

My mint has completely taken over the herb bed lol. I've got rooted cuttings in little pots if anyone local wants some for free. Not asking for postage or swaps, just don't want to compost them 🙂
Dahlia tuber surplus! I dug up more than I have room for and I'd rather give them away than store them all winter. Free to a good home, I'm just north of Bakersfield. Comment if interested.

Seed giveaway: I've got leftover packets of basil, cilantro and nasturtium from last year, still good. Free to anyone who wants them, I'll leave them at the community garden gate. No catch, no postage, just want them used before they go stale.
Have a bunch of extra pepper seedlings, jalapeno plus one mystery hot variety, looking for homes. Completely free, I just hate tossing healthy starts. I'm in the Denver metro if anyone's nearby 🌱

Anyone in the Portland area want some tomato seedlings? I started way too many San Marzanos and they're getting leggy on the windowsill. Free, just come grab them, no money or anything. DM me if you're close 🍅
Digging up my hostas this weekend to redo the bed, got about a dozen divisions going spare. Happy to hand them off to whoever wants them, nothing needed in return. I'm in zone 6b near Springfield.
Offering strawberry runners free - my patch threw out way too many this spring and they're crowding everything. You'd need to pick them up in town here, no charge obviously. First come first served.
Giving away a big aloe vera pup and a few spider plant babies. Nothing wanted for them, just pay it forward someday. Message me, I'm around the Raleigh area.

Giving away raspberry canes, my row has spread into the path and I've dug up about 15 suckers. They're free, take as many as you like, I'll even wrap them in damp newspaper for the trip home. My other half says I'm a plant hoarder and wants them gone before the weekend 😂

I saved WAY too many tomato seeds this year (San Marzano and Black Krim) and I've got about 40 little envelopes sitting on the windowsill doing nothing. Free to anyone who wants them, nothing needed in return, not even a stamp, I'll cover postage. Just DM me your details and I'll get them out this week 🙂 I'm in Aus so if you're overseas they might take a while.

Free chilli seedlings! I germinated 24 habanero and jalapeno seeds expecting half to fail and of course every single one came up. They're about 4 inches tall now in wee pots and I've run out of windowsill. Free to good homes, nothing asked, message me if you're near Manchester and can collect.

Anyone in the Ottawa area want some rhubarb crowns? Dividing the bed this weekend and I'll have 4 or 5 spare. They're yours free, I just don't want to compost them. Bring a bag and a trowel, I'll leave them sitting by the shed for whoever gets here first.

Spider plant babies up for grabs! My big one has gone absolutely mental this spring and I've got 12 little rooted plantlets in jars on the kitchen bench. No charge, no catch, I just can't bring myself to bin them. Pickup from the northern beaches if you're local, otherwise I can post a couple out.

Lemon balm and mint cuttings going spare if anyone wants them. They root in water in about a week, honestly too easy, and I've got far more than I know what to do with. Free, nothing in return, just give me a shout and I'll stick some in the post.

Offering up some dahlia tubers, Cafe au Lait, Labyrinth and a few unnamed ones I've lost the labels for. Nothing wanted for them, this is just me being completely overrun this year. First come first served, DM me and I'll set some aside for you.

I've got about half a kilo of mixed wildflower seed left over from a big packet and it's way more than my patch will ever need. Happy to split it into envelopes and send them out free to whoever wants some. No money, no strings, I just hate seeing it go to waste 🌸

subtopic: Local shop recommendations without links or codes

subtopic: Product recommendations without links or codes

subtopic: Product recommendations without links or codes

subtopic: Product recommendations without links or codes

subtopic: Product recommendations without links or codes
text: Shoutout to Pemberton Seeds - sowed their cavolo nero and germination was near enough 100%, packet says sow by 2027 which is mad. Nothing in it for me, just genuinely impressed with them.

Lost one of my old hens to a fox last night, feeling rotten about it. The run has a gap I didn't notice near the gate. Just a reminder to check your fencing before the weather turns. She was a good layer and a bossy old thing.

Anyone else use their chickens to clear a veg bed at the end of the season? I let my four girls into the old brassica patch for a week and they absolutely demolished the slugs and leftover leaves. Only downside is they scratched up the mulch something awful 😅 Do you fence them off or just let them go to town?

My chickens have basically tilled my flower border for me. I didn't ask them to, but they've scratched it into a fine seedbed and now I'm wondering whether to just plant squash there. Has anyone else given up and let the birds design the garden? 😂

Do any of you feed your chickens garden scraps? Mine go mental for tomato ends and cucumber peel, but I read somewhere that too much can upset them. I've been keeping it to a small bowl in the afternoon. Curious what works for others.

Bit of a weird one - my neighbour's chickens keep hopping the fence and dust bathing in my herb bed. I don't mind the eggs they leave as payment but the rosemary is suffering. How do you politely chicken-proof a shared boundary? No drama, just want my thyme back.

My hen went broody right in the middle of the compost heap and I can't move her without a fight. She's sitting on nothing but she's determined. Any tricks to break a broody without being cruel? I've tried the cool crate but she just looks at me like I've personally offended her.

The girls have decided my newly planted kale is a buffet. Little monsters got through the netting overnight. Any recommendations for a taller barrier that doesn't look like Fort Knox? I love them but I also want to eat something this winter.

Chicken poop question - I've been adding the bedding from the coop to the compost bin, is that ok or does it need to sit longer before it goes on the beds? Don't want to burn my tomatoes next spring. Coop is pine shavings if that matters.
My bees have been grumpy as hell this week with the heat. Even the lavender isn't keeping them calm. I'm watering the garden at dusk and leaving them alone. Do yours get moody in a heatwave too? 😅

Finally got my beekeeping suit and it's a game changer. Way less nervous going near the hive now. Also doubles as a decent gardening jacket for pruning the thorny stuff lol. Anyone else use theirs for general garden jobs?

Checked the hive today and found the queen, felt like winning the lottery lol. The garden is full of borage and the bees are loving it. Do you lot plant extra flowers just for your bees or just let them get on with it?
Saw a big swarm in the apple tree this morning and managed to coax it into a box. No idea what I'm doing tbh but they seem settled. Fingers crossed they stay. Anyone got tips for a new beekeeper?
Random question: is it safe to use neem oil on the veg beds if I've got a hive nearby? Don't want to hurt the bees. I usually spray in the evening but not sure if that's enough.

Extracted my first honey at the weekend! Only 4 jars but I'm stupidly proud. The kitchen smelled amazing. Already planning to expand the apiary next spring, maybe add another two hives near the fruit trees.

First year with bees and I'm already hooked 🐝 Hive is at the bottom of the veg patch and the girls are all over the runner beans. Anyone else notice better pollination since getting a hive? I'm in zone 6b if that matters.

Bit of a weird one but does anyone here keep bees? I've got a nuc coming next month and I'm trying to work out where to put it so it doesn't annoy the neighbours. Thought the sunny corner by the compost heap might work but not sure about the wind.
Dried a tray of my thai chilies in the oven overnight and forgot to open a window. Whole house was coughing at 6am lol. Peppers came out great though, ground them into flakes.
Third batch of sauerkraut on the go, this one's the last of the winter cabbage plus a bit of my own caraway. Crock's sat in the corner stinking the kitchen out, other half not impressed 😂
Quick pickled the cucumber glut with vinegar, dill off the windowsill pot and a spoon of honey. Two jars already gone. Neighbour asked for the recipe so I scribbled it on the back of a seed packet.
Green tomato chutney bubbling away, using up all the ones that never ripened before the frost hit. Added raisins and a splash of the cider we brewed. House smells like vinegar and cloves, love it.
Simmered down 6kg of plum tomatoes into passata, sieved twice and bottled hot. Got 7 bottles cooling on the counter and the whole flat smells amazing. Nothing beats your own sauce in january.
Made 14 jars of strawberry jam yesterday from the patch out back, kitchen still smells like sugar. Anyone else's berries going absolutely mental this year? 🍓
Pressure canned 9 quarts of San Marzano today, first go with the new gauge. Took me all afternoon but the shelf looks proper now. Do you lot add lemon juice or just trust the acidity?
Blanched and froze about 4kg of french beans off the allotment. Ran out of freezer bags so half are in old ice cream tubs. Reckon they'll be alright till february?

Made a new handle for my grandad's old hoe out of an ash branch I'd had drying in the garage. It's not pretty but it fits my hand better than the original. Rubbed it with linseed oil and now it smells like a cricket bat.

Picked up an old Spear & Jackson fork at a car boot sale for £4, absolutely caked in rust. Spent yesterday with wire wool and oil and it's come up lovely, though the handle still needs a rub down. Anyone else rescue tools like this or am I just tight? 😅

Finally sharpened my secateurs with a diamond file instead of just hacking at things. What angle do you all use? I gave them a quick go on the buddleia and it's like a different tool, slightly worried I've overdone it.

My daughter bought me a hori-hori for my birthday and I honestly don't know how I gardened without it. It's brilliant for dandelions and planting bulbs, and I may have slept with it in my back pocket by accident. Do you sharpen yours often?

Borrowed a neighbour's long-handled bulb planter for my spring bulbs and now I really want one. Any recommendations for a decent one that won't bend at the first sight of clay? No links please, just names you've actually used.

My wheelbarrow tyre keeps going flat and it's driving me up the wall. I only use it for compost and moving pots, nothing heavy. Has anyone tried the solid foam inserts or should I just patch the inner tube again?

Do you oil your pruning shears after every use or just at the end of the season? Mine got sticky sap all over the pivot and now they squeak like a mouse. I've cleaned them but not sure if 3-in-1 oil is a bad idea.

Random one, but does anyone else use a cheap silicone spatula to scrape mud off their trowels before it sets? My partner thinks I've lost it, but it gets right into the corners without scratching. Hose them off after, obviously.

My orchid has finally rebloomed after two years of doing nothing! I nearly binned it last winter but a friend said to give it a cooler spot by the window. Just wanted to share because I'm ridiculously pleased 🌸

My monstera has been putting out aerial roots like crazy since I moved it to the east window. Is it ok to tuck them back into the pot or should I leave them alone? Feels like it's trying to escape lol 🌿

Just repotted my ficus into a bigger pot and now it's dropping leaves like no tomorrow. I used a mix with extra perlite but maybe I watered too soon? Any advice would be great, I'm a bit gutted as it was doing so well.

Anyone else's calathea go absolutely dramatic when the heating comes on? Mine has crispy edges again and I'm wondering if a pebble tray actually helps or if it's just a myth. I'm in Manchester so it's proper grim and damp outside but the radiators are brutal.
Bit of a weird one but do you lot talk to your houseplants? I swear my pothos grows faster when I tell it it's doing a good job. My partner thinks I've lost it 😂

My cat has decided the spider plant is her personal salad bar. I've moved it up high but she's now using the bookshelf as a climbing frame. Any pet-safe houseplants that can survive a determined tabby? Also is it normal for cats to be obsessed with ponytail palms?

I've got a south-facing windowsill that gets full sun all afternoon and I'm struggling to find a plant that won't scorch. Would a snake plant cope or is it better somewhere shadier? Not fussed about flowers, just want something alive by spring.

Can we talk about how expensive nice terracotta pots have got? I went to a garden centre in Leeds and nearly fell over at the price of a 20cm pot. Ended up using old yoghurt pots for cuttings instead. Do cuttings care what they're potted in or is it just aesthetics?

so my neighbour's rabbit got out and spent a happy afternoon in my lettuce patch. i'm not even mad, it was comical. i've fenced the veg with chicken wire now but do i need to worry about anything it might have left behind on the leaves?

little win: put a small shallow dish of water under the bird bath and now the dog drinks from it instead of trampling my strawberries. not pretty but it works. also the blackbirds seem to like it so everyone's happy

does anyone else's dog eat the tomatoes straight off the vine? mine only goes for the ripe ones, which honestly is a bit insulting. i've got 6 plants and i think i've harvested maybe 3 tomatoes this whole summer.

our rescue greyhound keeps cutting the corner on the path and flattening my lavender. its not his fault, he's a big lad and the beds are narrow. has anyone had luck with those low edging things or do i just need to move the plants back further?

my tortoise lives outside in the summer and he's absolutely demolished the hostas by the shed. i knew he'd nibble but i didnt think he'd take them down to stumps overnight. any plants that are safe for him to eat that also look decent?

first time letting the hens... sorry, wrong - first time letting the CAT out into the new garden and shes been chewing on something. is there anything common in a UK garden that's dangerous to cats? i've got foxgloves and some lilies in pots and now im paranoid

my cat has decided the new raised bed is her personal litter tray 🙃 i've tried netting over it but she just sits on the netting and looks at me. any ideas that dont involve yelling at her all day? i'm in southern ontario if that matters, zone 5b

question about snail bait and dogs - my sister's lab got into the pellets last year and it was a horrible vet bill. i've switched to beer traps and hand picking but the slugs are winning this wet spring. what do you all use that's safe with a nosy dog around?

The cactus on my windowsill has a flower bud for the first time in four years. Four years of just sitting there looking smug and now this little pink thing appears. I've become one of those people who photographs a plant daily, no regrets 🌵

Tiny first rose bud on the climber I thought I'd killed last summer! It's only one flower and kind of ragged, but I'm taking it as a personal triumph. I might have overwatered everything else in celebration. Oops.

Went out to check the tulips and the first one is properly open! Bright orange, slightly wonky, absolutely perfect to me. The wind has already battered it a bit so I've been out there clucking around it like a hen. No self-control when blooms start.

Sweet corn is tasseling and the first cucumber flowers are out at the allotment. Everything looks a bit chaotic but it's finally happening. Neighbour says my beds look like a plant jumble sale, which is fair. Still thrilled though.

First dahlia opened today!! I've been checking it every morning like a lunatic 😅 It's a deep burgundy one I grew from a tuber at the spring swap. No idea what variety but I'm obsessed. Also the slugs have ignored it so far, which feels suspicious.

My sweet peas finally started flowering and the whole wigwam smells amazing. I planted them late because I forgot where I'd put the seeds lol. Only three blooms so far but I keep dragging my partner out to sniff them. He is not as thrilled as I am 🌸

I tried to be organised and write labels in permanent marker, but apparently “permanent” means “until one watering”. Now I have a mystery bed of seedlings and I’m just going to wait and see what happens. Surprise gardening!

I got all excited about my first ever carrot harvest and pulled up... one tiny orange nub and a lot of very healthy roots 😂. The compost got most of them. On the plus side, the tops made a nice garnish.

I finally admitted defeat to the slugs. My lettuce seedlings lasted about 12 hours before becoming a slimy buffet 🐌. Next year I’m growing everything in pots on the table, or maybe just growing rocks.

First time trying winter squash and I somehow managed to plant them way too close together. The patch is now a giant wrestling match of vines and I can’t find the fruit. Lesson learned, I guess. Has anyone else created a squash jungle by accident?

Note to self: don’t “just quickly” transplant tomatoes at 7pm in July and then forget to water them. Came out this morning to six sad little wilted sticks. Any chance they bounce back or should I start planning their funeral? 🍅

My seed trays were doing so well until I left them outside for “a bit of fresh air” and came back to a wind disaster. Soil everywhere, labels gone, and I have no idea which pepper is which now. Gardening keeps me humble.

Finally pulled the garlic today and got 23 decent bulbs, plus a bunch of tiny ones I’ll pretend were intentional 🙃 zone 6b, planted last October. The biggest bulb was almost the size of my fist, which is good because my actual fists are tiny. Curing them on the porch now and trying not to eat them all before winter.

The zucchini is out of control. I picked three today and there are two more that look like they could be used as doorstops. Neighbor took one, looked at the second and suddenly remembered he had somewhere to be 😂. Anyone else drowning in squash? I'm running out of creative hiding spots.

First real tomato harvest!! 🍅 Only 4 ripe ones but I'm stupidly proud. The cherries split after that rain, so I picked them early and made a tiny batch of sauce. It was more like tomato paste with ambitions lol. Next year I'll stake them better, maybe.

Pumpkin update: got two decent sugar pumpkins off the vines before the frost. The third one is still green and stubborn, so it's living on the kitchen windowsill now like a houseplant. My partner says it's not decor, but I disagree. Roasted the first one yesterday and the kitchen smelled amazing.

Harvested my first ever crop of bush beans this morning! Just a colander full, but they tasted so good with butter. My kid helped pick them and ate half raw before we got inside. Already planning a bigger patch next year, maybe with some purple ones for fun.

Not a great year for my peppers, ngl. The bell peppers are tiny and one plant just made one sad little pepper that turned red immediately. The jalapeños did okay though, got about a dozen. I'm calling it a win because nothing died.

Seed starting update: the brassicas are leggy as hell, the tomatoes are thriving, and the cosmos are doing whatever they want. Gardening is humbling. Also I may have knocked an entire tray off the shelf this morning, so there's that.
Checked my milk jug winter sowing setup today and the kale has germinated! In February! I'm in Minnesota so this feels like a minor miracle. The spinach is still sleeping but I have hope.

Started my tomato seeds on the windowsill three weeks ago and they're finally poking through! Only 4 out of 12 so far but I'm taking it as a win. My cat seems to think the seed trays are a bed though 😅

Note to self: don't start 60 pepper plants 'just in case'. My kitchen table is now a jungle and my partner is threatening to move out. Anyone in zone 7 want some seedlings? Free, obviously, just come get them.
Does anyone else talk to their seedlings? I've been giving mine daily pep talks and honestly they look better than last year's batch. Maybe it's the grow light, maybe it's the emotional support 🤷

Well, my first attempt at starting seeds indoors was a total bust. I used regular potting soil instead of seed mix and now I've got fungus gnats everywhere. Lesson learned the hard way lol. Round two starts this weekend.

The courgettes have officially taken over the veg patch. I went out to pick one and came back with three marrows and a mild sense of panic. Neighbours are locking their doors when they see me with a carrier bag 😂
Update on my balcony chillies: three tiny green ones after months of staring at flowers. I feel like a proud but slightly useless parent. Now if only I could stop checking them every 10 minutes.
Planted my first ever tomato seedlings in March and I’ve already killed half of them by overwatering 🤦‍♀️ The survivors are looking smug though. Any tips for a serial plant drown-er?

My carrot bed came up as a lovely patch of... something. Pretty sure it's mostly weeds with a few carrots hiding out of shame. Still calling it a success because I didn't trip over the hose this time.

First dahlias opened this week! I bought the tubers on a whim and forgot where I planted them, so this is a nice surprise. The slugs have had a nibble but honestly same, it's been a wet summer here in the UK.

Repotted my monstera and somehow ended up with more soil on the floor than in the pot. It's now leaning like it's had a long week. Fingers crossed it forgives me and doesn't drop every leaf in protest.
Oh, you've been gardening for 30 years? 😂😂 And you still can't tell a weed from a seedling. Maybe take up knitting.

Thanks for the 'help' with my houseplants. They're all dead now. 🙃🙃 Maybe stick to plastic ones.
